purpose: 2D visual drafts for approval before modeling

drafts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: a 2D stained-glass design draft to later become a multicolor PLA insert, portrait aspect ratio 108.2:144.2. Use the two attached dog photographs only as subject/identity references, not as a background or edit target. Preserve this particular male corgi mix: very large upright ears with gently rounded tips, warm golden-tan face, noticeably long tapered muzzle (not a short purebred corgi muzzle), black nose, soft brown almond-shaped attentive eyes, subtle dark outer-eye markings, pale cream around the mouth/chin and chest, and darker brown/black saddle behind the head. Convey his gentle, inquisitive attentiveness to his human, not an aggressive or goofy expression. He is an adult dog with puppy-dog eyes, not a baby puppy.
Style: bold, charming, deliberately simplified stained glass. Flat solid color pieces separated by clean, substantial black lead lines; broad elegant curved shapes, a few angular panes. A continuous moderate-width BLACK outer rectangular border on all four edges, approximately 2.5% of panel width, with black reaching the very outside edge. Entire panel shown straight on, uncropped. White outside margin only if needed. No perspective mockup, no photographed glass texture, no photorealism, no fur hairs, no gradients, no metallic glints, no microfacets. All details must be plausible to adapt for a 108 mm wide 0.4 mm nozzle printed panel: roughly 20–35 major colored shapes, no hairlines or tiny slivers, black joins connected to the larger leading network, small eye catchlights restrained and large enough to print. Use a tight six-color palette: black, cocoa brown, warm caramel tan, pale cream, warm white, and cyan-blue. Tan/cream ears instead of adding pink. Keep the subject recognizable from the photos and keep his forehead broad enough, ears full-sized, muzzle slender but not pinched. A simple cyan-blue background split into just 4–6 large panes. No human, furniture, lettering, labels, watermark, paw-print ornaments or extraneous animals. Output ONE finished draft panel.
COMPOSITION A — “The attentive supervisor”: an almost frontal head-and-upper-chest portrait, oversized upright ears fully inside frame, subtle 10 degree head tilt, both warm eyes looking slightly upward at the viewer as if checking on his seated human. Closed mouth, soft relaxed expression, broad forehead, long cream-tipped muzzle. Dog occupies 78% of width with a small cyan margin around the ear tips. Lead lines support the head and chest and join the border. This is the most immediately readable, iconic choice.

COMPOSITION B — “At your side”: three-quarter head portrait turned toward the viewer's right, chin slightly raised and eye looking up/right toward his human, inspired specifically by photograph 2. Both ears visible, nearer ear large and open. Capture the devoted, quiet look of a dog sitting beside his human, without including the human or chair. Include a little upper chest and one broad cocoa-brown shoulder/saddle shape. Clearly three-quarter, not a flat side silhouette; visible near eye expressive and far eye only if anatomically natural. Gentle curves in the blue background suggest an arch while staying within a rectangular black frame.

COMPOSITION C — “The puppy-dog look”: head viewed gently from above, as in photograph 1, nose lowered a little while both eyes look upward toward the viewer, creating the tender attentive puppy-dog expression. Two big upright ears fan outward, generous broad forehead tapers into his characteristic longer muzzle and black nose. Head and small section of dark-backed shoulders fill the panel; not a full body. Mouth closed and neutral, very soft inner brows, ears alert. Use slightly more geometric, broad stained-glass facets than A and B, but no realistic fur. Background has broad diagonal blue panes framing the two ears.
